passages.context: The daily entries that carry parenthetical Ordinary Time week numbers: the Monday after the Baptism of the Lord, which opens the First Week, and the entries in the days after Pentecost that name the week resumed after Easter Time and the weeks following it. Together with the pre-Lenten Sunday entries they fix the last week used before Lent and the first week resumed after Pentecost for this year.
passages.notes: Read in the extracted text layer of the exact acquired PDF. passages.context: The front-matter tables headed Principal Celebrations of the Liturgical Year 2028, Cycles - Lectionary for Mass, and Liturgy of the Hours, together with the introductory paragraphs that describe how the cycles were applied. They give the two First Sundays of Advent bounding the year, Ash Wednesday, Easter, the Thursday Ascension, Pentecost, the Sunday Most Holy Body and Blood of Christ, the Sunday and weekday Lectionary letters with their exact intervals, and the volumes and week spans of the Liturgy of the Hours.

work.author: United States Conference of Catholic Bishops, Secretariat of Divine Worship
work.description: The annual calendar published by the Secretariat of Divine Worship for the dioceses of the United States of America, resolving the General Roman Calendar and the Proper Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States of America for one liturgical year. Each civil year is a distinct edition. It is a competent territorial witness to a year's resolution, not the promulgating source of the recurring proper calendar.
work.title: Liturgical Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States of America
